en: Before we send you on any serious assignments, we need to make sure your equipment can handle the environment. Lunar conditions are considerably different from those on Earth. Temperature fluctuations, radiation exposure, and the station's damaged infrastructure may interfere with some of your equipment. I want you to remain deployed for at least five minutes. That's all. Don't rush back to extraction. We need sufficient field data to determine whether your equipment can withstand prolonged exposure. Good luck out there.

Five minutes. Good, that's enough for an initial assessment. Your equipment appears to have performed within acceptable parameters. There are still some irregularities in the recorded readings, but nothing that warrants immediate concern. We'll continue monitoring its performance during future deployments. Consider this your first successful field test.

Now that we've established your equipment can handle the environment, it's time to test the reason you're carrying that weapon. As you already know, conventional firearms are ineffective against the entities occupying the station. That's precisely why the Battle Halo program was developed. We've conducted extensive laboratory testing, but simulated results can only tell us so much. I want five confirmed eliminations using your Battle Halo. Make sure the weapon is functioning properly and report any irregularities you encounter. Let's see what our new toys can do.

Five confirmed eliminations. Excellent. The weapon's performance appears to be consistent with our laboratory predictions. The energy discharge successfully disrupted the specimens' biological structure. There are still some questions regarding how different specimen types respond to the weapon, but we'll investigate that later. For now, the results are satisfactory. Keep that weapon close. You're going to need it.

We've gathered enough information to establish that the entities are hostile. What we don't know is why. Their behavior is far from typical. Some specimens appear to attack anything that enters their vicinity, while others exhibit more coordinated responses. We need to understand what we're dealing with. Take these collection containers with you. You'll need to retrieve biological samples from three different specimens. Tissue, organic residue, whatever you can safely collect. Just make sure the samples are properly sealed. Our research department will handle the analysis.

Three samples. That's exactly what we needed. I'll have them transferred to the biological research department immediately. Preliminary observations suggest significant cellular abnormalities. Some of the samples also appear to retain traces of the energy signature associated with Battle Halo technology. That's interesting... Anyway, you've done your part. The researchers should be able to tell us more once they've completed their analysis.

Before we start digging through the station's infrastructure, I'd like you to look for something a little more personal. Research personnel were required to document their daily activities using portable information tablets. These devices stored individual reports, observations, and incident records. Most of the station's personnel are... unavailable. Their equipment, however, should still be somewhere inside. Find one of those tablets. I want to know what happened during the final days before the incident.

You've recovered a tablet? Good. I've reviewed the data. Most of the entries are routine research documentation, but the final reports are... concerning. Several personnel reported irregularities in specimen behavior. Others mentioned unauthorized experiments and unexplained security lockdowns. Interesting. None of this appears in the official incident report. Keep looking. There's something we're not being told.

The personnel tablets have given us a general picture of what happened. But personal reports aren't enough. We need to know what was happening at the administrative level. I've prepared a flash drive capable of extracting data from the station's older computer systems. Your target is the administrator's personal workstation. It should contain internal correspondence, security reports, and operational logs from before the catastrophe. Take the drive with you, connect it to the computer, and retrieve the data. And one more thing. Don't waste time exploring files unrelated to the incident. We only need information concerning the station's final operational period.

The extraction is complete. Let me see what we have... Hmm. These records indicate that the station's management was aware of the specimen instability long before the incident. There are multiple reports requesting an immediate suspension of the research program. Every request was denied. Even stranger, the security department received orders to restrict personnel movement several hours before the first reported containment breach. This wasn't an unexpected accident. Someone knew something was coming.

I've reviewed the administrative records. What we've found raises more questions than answers. The station was conducting research on something far beyond the scope of its publicly documented operations. We need the original research files. Not summaries, not personnel reports. The actual data. I've prepared a high-capacity storage drive capable of copying the station's research database. It won't be a quick process, so make sure the area is secure before initiating the transfer. Retrieve everything you can find and bring it back. This information is extremely sensitive. Under no circumstances should it fall into the wrong hands.

You've recovered the entire database? Excellent. This is... considerably more than we expected. The research files confirm that the specimens weren't simply being studied. They were being modified, tested, and deliberately exposed to experimental energy sources. There are also references to a project involving the Battle Halo technology. Wait... These records indicate that the company was aware of the connection between the specimens and the energy signatures emitted by the halos. That's impossible. The Battle Halo program was supposedly developed as a response to the incident. ... I need some time to review this information. For now, you've done your job. Don't discuss these findings with anyone.

You've probably noticed that your Battle Halo is capable of more than just defensive and offensive applications. One of its lesser-known functions is its ability to temporarily reconfigure its energy structure into a storage container. This feature was originally designed for transporting sensitive equipment and research materials without exposing them to the surrounding environment. I'd like you to put it to practical use. Take this mission package, store it inside your Halo, and bring it back with you. We need to confirm that the container configuration remains stable throughout an entire deployment.

The package arrived intact? Excellent. The container configuration appears to be functioning as intended. No significant energy fluctuations were detected during transportation. This could prove extremely useful for recovering sensitive materials from contaminated environments. I expect we'll be making frequent use of this function in the future.

We've received promising results from the stationary deployment tests. As you know, your Battle Halo can be detached and positioned independently. This allows it to perform several functions without requiring constant user input. For this assignment, we're interested in its automated defense capabilities. I want you to deploy your Halo in turret mode and use it to eliminate three hostile entities. Choose your deployment position carefully. The Halo needs a clear line of sight, and its energy reserves won't last forever. Let's see how well it performs without you having to pull the trigger yourself.

Three confirmed eliminations by the automated turret? Very good. The results indicate that the targeting system is capable of identifying and engaging hostile biological entities without direct operator intervention. This could make stationary deployment extremely valuable when securing extraction points or defending research areas. Just remember that automated defense still consumes Halo energy. Don't expect it to protect you indefinitely.
zh: 在安排正式任务前，我们得确认你的装备能适应研究站的环境。月面和地球不同，温差、辐射，还有站内受损的设施，都可能干扰装备。你要在战区待满五分钟，就这么简单。别急着去撤离点。我们需要足够的现场数据，才能判断装备能不能长时间运转。祝你好运。
五分钟。很好，够做初步评估了。你的装备在允许范围内正常运转。读数有一点异常，目前还不用担心。后续部署我们会继续监测。你的第一次现场测试通过了。
装备通过了环境测试。现在来测你手里的武器。常规枪械对站内的污染体效果很差，战斗光环就是为此研发的。实验室已经测过很多次，模拟终归代替不了实战。用战斗光环确认消灭五个目标。留意武器有没有异常，有问题就报回来。看看这些新家伙到底行不行。
确认消灭五个。很好。武器表现和实验室预测一致。能量释放破坏了样本的生物结构。不同类型的样本会有什么反应，还得再研究。现阶段结果合格。把武器带在身边，后面用得上。
我们知道那些东西有敌意，还不知道原因。有些一见人就攻击，有些会配合行动。这些反应都不寻常。带上采样容器，从三具不同的遗骸中取样。组织也好，残留物也好，安全取出来并封严。后面的分析交给研究部门。
三份样本，正好。我会马上转交生物研究部。初步观察发现了明显的细胞异常。部分样本似乎还残留战斗光环的能量特征。有意思。你这边的工作完成了。等分析结束，研究人员会给出更多结果。
在查站内设施之前，先找点个人记录。研究人员每天都要用便携平板写日志，日常工作、观察和异常事件都会存进去。站内大多数人员……联系不上了。不过他们的装备应该还在。带一台回来。我想知道事故前最后几天发生了什么。
找到了平板？好。我看过数据了。大多是常规研究记录，最后几篇却不太对劲。有人提到样本行为异常，也有人记录了未经批准的实验和原因不明的封锁。奇怪，这些在官方报告里一条都没有。继续找。还有事情瞒着我们。
个人平板让我们大概知道了经过，不过还得查管理层。我准备了一枚能从旧系统读数据的U盘。目标是管理员的私人工作站。里面应该还有事故前的内部邮件、安保报告和运行日志。把U盘接上，提取记录。还有，跟事故无关的文件别花时间。只需要研究站运行的最后一段。
提取完成。我看看。嗯……记录显示，管理层早就知道样本不稳定。报告里多次要求立刻暂停研究，全部被驳回了。更奇怪的是，首次收容失守前几个小时，安保部就接到限制人员通行的命令。这场事故并不突然。有人早就知道要出事。
我看过管理日志了。站内研究的范围远超对外公布的内容。现在需要原始研究文件。取原始数据，个人报告和摘要已经够了。我准备了一块高容量硬盘，可以拷贝研究站的数据库。传输要一段时间，开始前先确认周围安全。能带回来的都带回来。这些资料非常敏感，必须直接交回公司。
整个数据库都带回来了？很好。内容比预期多得多。资料显示，他们对样本进行了改造、测试，还故意让样本接触实验能源。这里也提到了战斗光环项目。等等……公司早就知道样本和光环的能量特征有联系。怎么会？光环不是事故发生后才开发的吗？……我得再看一遍。你完成了任务。这些发现先别对外说。
你应该已经发现，光环不只能攻击和防御。它可以暂时改变能量结构，展开成收纳空间。这个形态原本用来运送敏感设备和样本，隔绝外部环境。现在实地试一次。带上封存包，把它装进光环，再带回来。我们要确认收纳形态在整次部署中能保持稳定。
封存包完好无损？很好。收纳形态运转正常，途中没有明显能量波动。这个功能很适合从污染区回收敏感材料。以后应该会经常用到。
固定部署测试的初步结果不错。你可以把光环移到指定位置，让它独立照明、提供掩护，或者开火。这次切到炮塔模式，用它消灭三个目标。选一个视线开阔的地方。光环的能量有限，注意看余量。我们来看看它离开你之后表现如何。
炮塔确认消灭三个目标。很好。它可以自行识别并攻击敌对生物。以后守撤离点或研究区域，应该会派上用场。自动防御也会耗光环能量，别指望它一直开着。
